reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Code reading is correct: apply_to_chain_spec (chain_spec.rs:2311-2323) assigns fork epochs from config without validation, and fork_name_at_epoch (chain_spec.rs:334-355) uses first-match logic that would return wrong fork if epochs are out-of-order. However, this is a configuration validation issue, not a runtime vulnerability. Attack requires operator to manually load a malformed custom config file. Bug bounty scope explicitly excludes 'Configuration issues requiring operator error' and marks 'Local validator configuration' as semi-trusted and out-of-scope. All official network configs (mainnet altair=74240 < capella=194048 < deneb=269568; gnosis altair=512 < capella=648704 < deneb=889856) have properly ordered epochs. Not exploitable via P2P network or on-chain transactions. Spec cross-reference (fulu-fork/SG-001) defines fork trigger invariants but is silent on config validation, as this is an implementation-level concern. Severity calibrated to Informational per scope rules on operator-controlled configuration.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: Fulu Fork SG-001 (fork_trigger) defines fork trigger invariants but does not mandate config-time validation of epoch ordering; this is an implementation/operator concern.
